name: What should I do first if I think my Los Angeles soft-story apartment building needs seismic retrofitting?

mainEntity.name: What should I do first if I think my Los Angeles soft-story apartment building needs seismic retrofitting?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Start by confirming whether your building is on the city’s mandatory retrofit list and then get a professional structural evaluation. From there, you can prioritize scope, budget, and timing before committing to construction.

Los Angeles has ordinances that specifically target older soft-story wood apartments, with deadlines for submitting plans, obtaining permits, and completing work. Acting early gives you more contractor options and keeps you ahead of enforcement and potential penalties.

Key factors:
- Check city databases or your compliance order to confirm requirements and deadlines
- Hire a licensed structural engineer or design-build retrofit firm for an evaluation
- Request a phased plan and preliminary cost range
- Ask about tenant notification and possible temporary relocations

Don’t wait for a major earthquake or final warning notice; early planning usually means lower stress and more cost control. Use the evaluation to decide whether to do a minimum code retrofit or a more robust upgrade for long-term resilience.

An experienced LA-area retrofit provider can help you navigate both the engineering and the city paperwork from day one.
acceptedAnswer.description: First, confirm if your building is on Los Angeles’s mandatory soft-story retrofit list and what deadlines apply. Then hire a structural engineer or retrofit firm to evaluate the building, outline scope and costs, and help you plan permits, tenant communication, and a phased construction schedule.
